title: Security governance & reporting walkthrough - Northbridge Capital

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CSM) -- Evan Cole (Head of IT, Northbridge), Sara Mbaye (Security Lead), Diego Ruiz (Compliance), Anita Patel (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto): quick posture readout, access plan for compliance artifacts, SSO/roles and KMS flow questions, agreement on next steps.

00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving time during the holidays. I think we have about 50 minutes, we'll go through our SOC 2 and ISO artifacts, show how the compliance portal works, and then Liam will walk through RBAC/SSO and audit logs.
00:18 - Evan: thanks, yea we wanted this specifically to understand what evidence we can pull without extra engineering on our side, and to see how logs and keys flow for any dedicated/private deployment.
00:34 - Priya: quick agenda in chat, and I'll drop the compliance portal link after we provision access, just heads up it's read-only for external reviewers.
00:48 - Liam: cool, i'll start with the artifacts side — so we have a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO27001 cert in our portal, the SOC 2 is redacted for customer-specific data but includes control narratives, test procedures and findings. the ISO has scope and cert body details. sometimes the names in the PDF OCR get funky, sorry, it's auto-generated.
01:10 - Sara: when you say redacted, can you clarify what fields are removed? we need to confirm whether any CNIs or sample customer IDs are there, our auditor flagged that previously with other vendors.
01:25 - Liam: sure — we remove customer identifiers and any specific customer data samples; control narratives and the auditor opinion remain intact. i'll follow up with the redact policy doc; it's in the portal under Compliance -> Reports.
01:43 - Diego: and the portal — is it your Trust Center? how do we get access, and can we have separate roles? we have external auditors who need read-only access and internal reviewers who need more context.
01:57 - Maya: yes, we call it the compliance portal (trust center in older docs) — we can create role-based groups: reviewer, auditor, admin. Priya handles provisioning. external auditors get the reviewer group which is strictly read-only and cannot download raw logs unless we explicitly export them.
02:20 - Priya: on that note i'll need the list of emails for external auditors to add them as reviewer permission. also we can add expiration on access.
02:34 - Anita: question on download: auditors sometimes require raw syslog or CSV extracts of audit logs for a certain window. do you support exports in machine-friendly format?
02:48 - Liam: yes, we provide compressed CSV/NDJSON exports of audit traces — they include request IDs, model id, timestamp, latency and metadata. we have a retention policy default at 180 days for hosted, but for Dedicated/Private you can set retention longer; we can also stream logs to a customer S3 or GCS bucket. small caveat, PII is never stored in logs unless customer passes it — logging is configurable.
03:16 - Evan: how about chaining to our SIEM? we use Splunk and we need near-real-time log streaming for alerts. is that supported?
03:29 - Liam: yes — we have webhook and streaming connectors; for high-throughput setups we recommend the dedicated forwarder (we call it the log forwarder) or if you're in Private, you can install the local agent. sometimes the names in doc are misspelled as log-forwader in older exports, sorry.
03:50 - Sara: KMS and key ownership — we require CMKs in our own HSM for regulatory reasons. can you support envelope encryption where customer keys never leave our control?
04:06 - Liam: absolutely — for Private and Dedicated we support BYOK via KMS/HSM. we use envelope encryption: model payloads are encrypted with a data key that is encrypted under your CMK. the CMK can be in your cloud KMS or a partner HSM. for hosted we provide our own KMS but we do offer a customer-managed-key option for enterprise customers under contract.
04:34 - Diego: will we get an architecture diagram of that flow? auditors like to see sequence diagrams for key management.
04:42 - Liam: yes i'll supply a KMS flow diagram showing CSR, data key generation, envelope encryption and the path for logs. i'll also include where audit logs are emitted — KMS access logs, key usage events, etc.
04:56 - Maya: quick question for timeline — Evan, do you have a date that auditors start reviewing?
05:03 - Evan: earliest they might start is 2027-01-10 but internal reviewers will likely begin in late Dec. we want portal access this week if possible so we can get some eyes on the docs.
05:16 - Priya: we can provision read-only access by 2026-12-23. please send the list of emails.
05:28 - Anita: data residency — we need EU-only processing for a subset of workloads. how do you guarantee residency and separation?
05:39 - Liam: we have region pinning and routing policies — you can pin model serving to a region and we also support private deployments behind a customer VPC in the region. for strict residency we'd recommend Private (the on-prem or VPC private control plane). note that some third-party components like monitoring may still span regions unless isolated for Private.
06:01 - Sara: can you map which controls in SOC 2 map to our internal control objectives? we typically ask for a controls matrix.
06:12 - Maya: yes, we've got a controls mapping artifact that aligns SOC 2/ISO controls to common control objectives — we'll share that matrix. it's a spreadsheet with control IDs and control narratives.
06:25 - Diego: is that matrix already redacted or is there sensitive material in it?
06:30 - Liam: it's safe for external reviewers — it only maps which Redwood controls cover things like access control, change management, incident response, etc. I'll attach the mapping and also note which are shared responsibilities. sometimes the wording in docs shows "KV cache" as K-V cache which is silly but it's not material.
06:50 - Evan: what about SSO? we use Okta currently. we need SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning for groups so we can map our roles to Redwood roles.
07:02 - Liam: supported — SAML for auth and SCIM for user/group sync. RBAC mapping can be done either via group claims or SCIM. for auditors we recommend SCIM provisioning plus assertions for group membership to reduce manual sync. we'll provide sample IdP metadata and a test tenant.
07:22 - Sara: any constraints on session length, MFA requirements? auditors check that.
07:28 - Maya: we enforce session expiration and require MFA for admin accounts. for reviewer groups, we can enforce org-level MFA through SSO policy. we'll surface the exact values in the security policy doc.
07:40 - Anita: about raw evidence delivery — do you have a secure transfer process? we prefer SFTP with ephemeral creds or direct bucket access with short-lived tokens.
07:51 - Priya: we can push artifacts to a customer-controlled S3 with presigned URLs or use encrypted SFTP. we'll coordinate based on your preference.
08:03 - Evan: show me an example of audit log fields — what columns, are there IPs?
08:10 - Liam: sample CSV: timestamp, request_id, model_id, route, user_id (if available), region, latency_ms, status_code, request_size, response_size, kms_key_id (if encryption used), actor_type. IPs are optional and can be omitted for privacy; if you require IPs we can include them but it's configurable.
08:33 - Diego: retention again — hosted defaults 180 but our policy needs 365. can you set retention on a per-account basis?
08:40 - Liam: yes for Dedicated and Private yes; for hosted we offer extended retention as an addon. we can set to 365 for your account. I'll include pricing notes.
08:52 - Maya: competitors were mentioned in your RFI, did you want to discuss differences quickly?
08:58 - Evan: just to note CloudEndPoint and VaultAI asked similar questions — main concern is key ownership and portal visibility.
09:08 - Maya: good, we'll make sure the docs highlight BYOK and portal access granularity.
09:14 - (silence / typing)
09:30 - Liam: on the ISO scope question: some customers assume ISO covers all services — we clearly list service components in the cert scope. we'll share the exact scope doc, and if you need additional controls included for an enterprise purchase we can discuss a scope extension during contracting.
09:52 - Sara: incident response — do you provide breach notifications with SLAs? auditors want to see mean time to detect and respond.
10:00 - Liam: yes we have an IR playbook; notifications to customers for production-impacting incidents have defined timelines. i'll share the IR summary and MTTR metrics. note that exact MTTR varies by incident type.
10:16 - Diego: would you be able to provide raw evidence of configuration changes for a sample window? some auditors ask for change history tied to PRs.
10:25 - Priya: we can export change logs and link them to ticket IDs; we have a consolidated evidence package option that bundles logs, change records and policy docs for audit review.
10:40 - Evan: ok that helps. what's the smallest set of artifacts we need to give auditors to satisfy an initial review?
10:48 - Maya: typically: SOC 2 Type II report, auditor letter, ISO27001 cert and scope, controls mapping matrix, KMS flow diagram, sample audit log export, SSO configuration doc and an access list. we'll package that.
11:04 - Anita: on the networking front, for Private can we run behind our firewall with mutual TLS to your control plane?
11:12 - Liam: we support mutual TLS for dedicated private tunnels and allow customer-supplied certs. some older docs call it "mTLS tunnel" spelled odd, but yes it's supported.
11:25 - Diego: one compliance nit: we need assurance that archived backups are encrypted at rest and that key rotation is documented.
11:33 - Liam: backups are encrypted; rotation policies are documented in the key management policy. we can provide rotation logs and evidence of key rollover if you need.
11:45 - Evan: cool. let's recap next steps.
11:48 - Maya: recap — Redwood will: 1) provision portal access for reviewer list (Priya), 2) upload SOC2 + ISO docs (Maya), 3) deliver KMS flow and audit log samples (Liam), 4) coordinate SSO metadata exchange (Diego/Evan). timelines are as noted in chat. anything to add?
12:10 - Sara: please ensure the SOC2 is redacted per your policy, we will ask auditors but initial glance should be safe.
12:18 - Maya: noted.
12:22 - Diego: one more — pricing for extended retention and BYOK options, can you send that with the artifacts?
12:30 - Maya: yes i'll send a pricing appendix with the artifact bundle.
12:36 - Evan: thanks everyone, that's helpful. we'll expect the access by 12/23 and we'll circulate reviewers.
12:44 - Priya: i'll follow up with a provisioning email and expiration settings.
12:50 - Maya: great — thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifact bundle and next steps. Happy holidays.

End of meeting.

Notes: transcript contains typical minor transcription artifacts (mis-typed product names, occasional filler). References in chat to portal links and docs were promised; links not embedded in transcript for privacy.
